findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. The person in charge had a a certification that has expired and is enrolled for renewal in July. Ensure that there is always one certified food protection manager present at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn’t any paper towels available at the hand-sink located at the entrance of the deli bar. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided. Be sure that paper towels are available at every hand-sink to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION. The sanitizer solution in the sani bucket at the deli bar area was measured at 0 ppm at the beginning of the inspection. Staff was educated and the sani bucket was remade measuring at 200 ppm. Ensure that the sani bucket is monitored and changed at a regular frequency to ensure that food-contact surfaces are appropriately sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking on the triple sink in the kitchen was observed to be loose leaving the triple sink unsealed to the wall. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspectors that that the sink will be caulked appropriately. Ensure that the sink is re-caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.comment: (REPEAT x2) Observed a buildup of grease underneath and behind the fryers and other cooking equipment in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.

(B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed mop heads improperly stored on the floor of the mop sink and the mop bucket. Discussed with PIC and the mop heads were taken to be stored properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a knife stored on a magnetic knife holder to be soiled with debris inside of the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and knife was brought to the triple sink to be rewashed and sanitized. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed several dead mice on a glue board in the back-stock area. The facility is aware of the rodent issue. Pest control is done internally through Schnuck’s corporate. Ensure that the facility is free of rodent activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer bucket available in the kitchen area while cooking and food preparation was taking place. A sani bucket was created and tested at 200(q). Ensure that there is a sani bucket present during all hours of operation if food preparation is occurring.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: There is observed an accumulation of grease on the floor behind and underneath the fryer in the deli kitchen. Ensure the current grease accumulation is cleaned and then ensure this area is cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket at the start of the inspection was tested and was recorded less than 100ppm. The bucket was removed from service, dumped, and replaced with a fresh sanitizer solution from the dispenser. The new tested solution was tested and recorded at 200ppm. Ensure test strips are regularly utilized to ensure the sanitizer is testing appropriately.
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The magnetic knife holder is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on the top surface of the equipment. Ensure this surface is cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. PIC completed the cleaning and sanitizing of the knife holder during the inspection.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The wall next to the fryer in the kitchen is observed to have an accumulation of grease and food debris. Ensure the surfaces surrounding the fryers and other equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Employees of the deli are observed to not have completed the required food handler training courses. Ensure that all employees that handle food and equipment of the food service operation complete the necessary food handlers training course. 
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The triple sink in the deli kitchen is observed to be coming away form the wall and the caulking seal is no longer in good repair. The old caulking needs to be removed and new caulking needs to be placed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.comment:

The facility is to contact their company that performs maintenance on their chemical dispenser and utilize alternative sanitizers for their sanitizer bucket and wash, rinse, sanitize cycle until appropriate sanitizer concentrations can be met by the dispenser.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Beneath the sanitizer dispenser is a hole in the metal sink. Ensure this hole is patched to prevent soil residue and buildup through the hole.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The caulking by the deli triple sink and both hand sinks appears to be degrading and allowing water/debris accumulation. Ensure the current old caulking is removed and a fresh layer is applied to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. The sani bucket observed in the deli area is observed at less than 100 ppm Quat. Quat sanitizers should be at a minimum concentration of 200 ppm. Bucket was remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
1) Employee was observed entering the deli and briefly rinsed hands before attempting to put on gloves. Inspector questioned if she had washed her hands and she said she had in the restroom. It was discussed that proper hand washing must occur both in the restroom and again when entering the deli. 

2) Employee was observed touching face and then briefly washing hands for a few seconds before drying hands. Inspector stopped employee and requested 10-15 seconds of scrubbing with soap and employee stated that as many times as he washes his hands he doesn't do the 10-15 seconds. We discussed this in the back room and he stated that he needs to rinse the powder off from the gloves. We discussed that hand washing before glove use must occur.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Boneless chicken in the hot holding case in the back room was probed at 125-126F. The traditional wings in the pan behind probed at 134F. Chicken was cooked approximately one hour ago.  Employee stated that hot foods are over at 7 pm and leftovers are discarded so these will be time controlled until 7 pm and then discarded. Hot foods must be held at internal temperatures of 135F or above at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Chicken in the hot holding case in the back room was probed at internal temperatures of 124-128F. Two pans of chicken were reported to have been in this case when employee got here at 1pm. These were discarded during the inspection. Unit was turned up during the inspection and will be monitored and serviced.  3-501.16(A)(1)  (P)  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: 1) Observed olives with feta cheese, garlic cloves in oil and garlic stuffed olives on the olive bar that were stocked around 11 am and were probed at internal temperatures of 56-59F. 2) Observed deli salads in the open display cooler to be probed at internal temperatures of 47-51F. All of these items were discarded and these coolers will not be used unit they have been serviced and are holding foods at internal temperatures of 41F or below. 3-501.16(A)(2)  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: No thermometers are available in the open display case where deli salads were discarded. Digital thermometers were inactivated because they take temperatures at the coil. Provide conspicuously placed thermometers in each hot and cold holding unit. 4-204-112  (C)  Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed no thermometer in left hand side display hot holding. Provide thermometer.
findings.citation_text: 750.150(a) All hot units that contain potentially hazardous foods shall contain  a conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Scoop in the bulk container of chicken breading was broken and missing a handle. Discard and replace with a scoop with the handle extended out of food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers of sanitizer wipes throughout deli area. Sanitizer wipes should only be used cleaning off probe thermometers. Sanitizer buckets shall be used to sanitize surfaces.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
The following food contact surfaces were soiled: 1) deli slicer with food debris. Clean between uses. 2)cutting board on shelves in mop sink area 3)shelves holding cooking supplies in mop sink area. Wash, rinse, and sanitize all food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Wrapping station was soiled with food debris. Clean non food contact surface.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Bag being used to protect rotisserie chicken in walk in cooler is soiled and has holes. Discard and use bags once.
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Drain in the area with the mop sink is soiled. Clean drain.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Vent above 3 compartment sink in dish area had an accumulation of dust. Clean vent.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
The two white bulk food containers on the roller cart in the walk-in cooler had no labels to identify their contents.  Label the contents of each container.

750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Boxes and sacks of food in the two freezers below the clock in the kitchen were open exposing the food to condensation drips and debris from shelves above.  The boxes and sacks were closed during the inspection to CORRECT the violation.  Keep the food covered at all times.

750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
A single service cup / container was used in place of a scoop with a handle in the following bulk food in the kitchen:
  1.  spicy breading (REPEAT VIOLATION) 
  2.  chicken breading 
Remove the cup and container and use scoops with handles.  Store the scoops in the food with the handle up out of the food to minimize hand contact with the food.

750-290 Provide appropriate utensils for dispensing food (must have handle, no bowls used).

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Tongs in the deli were stored out of the hot/cold food.  Store the tongs in the hot or cold food.

750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
The following sinks have moldy/discolored caulk joints between the sinks and wall:
  1.  mop sink in the dish washing room of the kitchen
  2.  three pan sink in the deli area
Remove the old caulk, sanitize the gap, and re-caulk the gaps.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
  1.  small spice containers above the 2 pan sink in the kitchen
  2.  bottom inside of the left True freezer under the radio in the kitchen  (REPEAT VIOLATION)  
  3.  door seals on both freezers below the radio in the kitchen
  3.  white bulk chicken breading container in kitchen
  4.  yellow top on the spicy breading container in the kitchen
  5.  black plastic milk crates the spicy breading container was setting on
  6.  surfaces inside the doors of the 2 fryers and the fryer wheels (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  7.  frame of the aluminum cart in the walk-in cooler on which raw chicken is stored  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
 Clean these surfaces.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Cooking utensils were stored food side up and uncovered on a wire rack in the dish washing room.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
Store the utensils covered, inverted, or cover each shelf above with a plastic shelf liners that are smooth, non-absorbent, and is easily cleanable.

750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors were soiled:
  1.  under the kitchen fryers (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  2.  under the kitchen chicken broiler close to the wall  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  3.  black riser coming up out of the floor between the kitchen warmer and convection oven  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
Clean these floors and the riser and adjacent surfaces.

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.
